attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed open letter on his Substack. He is giving his own reading of the bill, not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'as I understand' qualifier, the 'latest version' scope and the 'out of the original developer's control' condition. Its content describes the bill, so 'observation' is the right kind, but the qualifier marks it as his tentative reading rather than a firm legal assertion.

contract.note: The contract fairly keeps his qualifier and does not narrow 'open-source models' to covered model derivatives, which he never did. Scoring it true or false would mean treating a qualified reading as a firm claim.

evidence.note: Official Assembly committee analysis dated 2024-06-18, before the post. It describes amendments that exclude derivatives outside the developer's control. It concerns proposed amendments, not the bill text in force on Aug 10, so it is context only.

Lawfare interview dated 2024-08-05 in which the bill's author says the shutdown duty ends once a model is no longer in the developer's possession. This is the author's own account of his bill, not the statutory text, so it is context only, though consistent with Marcus's reading.

reviews.rationale: Marcus framed this as his qualified understanding ('as I understand'), so under the hedging rule it is not scored. The packet also lacks the operative bill text: the legislative pages returned 403 errors. The committee analysis and the bill author's interview fit his reading but are context, not proof of the statute's meaning on Aug 10, 2024.
